The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "YES" at $9123, and the routine that called it at $9119 goes on.

Inline text after JSR $1583 at $9124: X=16, Y=12, colour fields $0B/$90, then 2 glyph codes and a zero terminator at $912D. The renderer masks each code to six bits and copies eight bytes from $1AE8 + 8*glyph. Decoded glyph sequence: 'NO'. It resumes execution at $912E. This draws NO dimmed, in the colours of the option not chosen: the YES-chosen state, $24=$FF.

Continuation after rendering YES highlighted and NO dimmed (the Y key or joystick left): writes $24=$FF, the YES choice, and returns to the input loop at $90F9. $9135 tests the N key and joystick right for the opposite selection; $9145 commits the selection: with $24=$FF it clears the play window and jumps to $9069, which awards the score, saves the level state and loads the next level; with $24=0 it clears the flags and restores the spawn. Inline text separates this continuation from the preceding code block.

Raise the sprite curtain over the play window and wait until it is gone. Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($8ECF), after a lost life ($9009) and after GAME OVER ($9044). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Reset mutable Central Park engine state each time an area is set up: its one caller is $8F23, in the area set-up routine that also runs at the start of play and after a lost life. Inputs: the active overlay and resident reset service. Outputs: timers, actor and object flags, arrays, and sentinels are restored to initial values. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad engine state. Hardware: none; the resident call (ResetEngineTickBaselines, $11F1) only copies the tick $E2 into $026C, $026E and $0277, and this body makes no direct I/O write.

Set up the status of a level as it starts. It clears $022B, $022C, $70, $89 and $A0, fills the 30 bytes at $3F92 that keep each area's enemy energy, and both energies ($0229, $022A) with $2C, a full bar, and sets $7A to $AD. It copies the item flags saved when the level began ($03B0-$03D7) over the live ones ($03D8-$03FF) and clears $03E9-$03F1 among them, then puts the score ($1CA0) and the clock's digits back from the saved copy ($03CC-$03D7). It sets $87 to $BF, clears $011B-$013E and draws panel picture 0 at both of its places (DrawUiImageRecord, $B411, with A = 0 and X = 0, then 1). It builds no scene or wall data. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the drawing routine's scratch.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $930B. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $930B whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($92BD), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Central Park record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8DF4). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Central Park scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $9330/$9355/$937A/$939F; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Central Park spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Central Park area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

37-byte transition-index stream ending at $932F, consumed from index 1 by $9256 and $A196. For each preceding area, scan through its $FF delimiter; the resulting index addresses the four 37-byte spawn arrays at $9330, $9355, $937A and $939F. $92B3 compares the player's place along the area's edge, worked out from the player's coordinates, against this stream's thresholds, while $A1A0 adds the exit number 0-3 that the script command chose ($A17A-$A186). $FF delimiters therefore participate in indexing and must not be removed as padding.

37 parallel transition records, $9330-$9354: destination area; $FF (entries 34 and 36) marks an exit that leaves the level: InstallSceneStateRecordX ($92BD) turns it into the level-exit request $02AF=$FF. $92CB installs the selected index into current area/player state and redraw latches. Shares index with the $930B transition-threshold stream.

37 parallel transition records, $9355-$9379: player X coordinate. $92CB installs the selected index into current area/player state and redraw latches. Shares index with the $930B transition-threshold stream.

37 parallel transition records, $937A-$939E: player Y coordinate. $92CB installs the selected index into current area/player state and redraw latches. Shares index with the $930B transition-threshold stream.

37 parallel transition records, $939F-$93C3: low three bits heading, upper nibble command. $92CB installs the selected index into current area/player state and redraw latches. Shares index with the $930B transition-threshold stream.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $B44A), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $A8F1), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset Central Park's transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8DFB), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Central Park playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $B5 to $86; A returns $B5. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for Central Park. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.

Inline text after JSR $1583 at $957C: X=17, Y=20, colour fields $03/$E6, then 6 glyph codes and a zero terminator at $9589. The renderer masks each code to six bits and copies eight bytes from $1AE8 + 8*glyph. Decoded glyph sequence: 'MODE  '. It resumes execution at $958A.
Mutable glyph byte inside the inline MODE text at $957F. $9579 changes this displayed glyph; the following zero terminates the text at $9589. Execution resumes at $958A, not through this byte.

Resume after the inline MODE display: $958A jumps to the remaining input scan at $9598. A $0267 value $7F sets death flag $B6; a nonzero $02B7 resamples input. The heading-one path then compares changing normalized control values with $95D6/$95D7, increments progress $BF, and sets $02AF=$FF after 18 matched transitions; other heading or mismatch clears progress. This is continuation code within the scanner, not text data.

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $95BB. Together with the next-byte alias $95D7 it stores 19 values $95D6-$95E8; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.
Expected next value of the 19-byte control sequence beginning at $95D6, read with the current progress X at $95C0. This is an overlapping indexed base, not another allocated array.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $9330 on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $96A6 go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($FEF9 to $FEFB) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

Copy the first compiled collision coordinate into its paired endpoint field for the selected Central Park object or scene-entry rule. Inputs: Compiled collision coordinate $FEF9 in the active Central Park play occupant. Outputs: $FEFB equals $FEF9; A contains the copied value and N/Z reflect it; C/V are preserved. Clobbers: A and N/Z; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Apply Central Park's remaining room-specific entrance initialization after the optional room-$0D test, which copies a collision coordinate ($FEF9 to $FEFB) instead when $03E9 is set.
Inputs: Y is the current room index. $03EB selects the conditional variants for rooms $10/$11; the AI-script installer at $AD35 (InstallAiScriptMarkedActive), color registers, and entrance state are initialized.
Outputs: Room $0A installs $76=1/$62=$B7/$63=$CD/$5E=$5A=0, writes $D025=6, $D026=$0B, and $6A/$6B=3. Room $0E installs $76=1/$62=3/$63=$CE/$5E=$5A=0, writes $D025=$0A, $D026=9, and $F8=1. Room $10 with $03EB=0 installs $76=1/$62=$1E/$63=$CE/$5E=$5A=0 and writes $D025=$0A/$D026=8. Room $11 with $03EB!=0 installs $76=1/$62=$25/$63=$CE/$5E=$5A=0, writes $D025=8/$D026=$0A, and $F8=8. Room $0F installs $76=1/$62=$3C/$63=$CE/$5E=$5A=0. Other cases return unchanged by this tail.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $5A/$5E/$62/$63/$76, $6A/$6B, $F8, and the listed VIC color registers on their exact room paths; Y is preserved, and the no-match path changes only comparison flags.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II sprite multicolor registers $D025/$D026 on rooms $0A, $0E, and the enabled $10/$11 variants; no CIA or SID access is performed by this dispatch tail.

Entrance animations, three bytes to an entry and $FF to end the list: the exit the player arrived by (its number in the exit tables at $9330 on), then the kind of entrance and how many animation steps it lasts, which ApplySceneEntryRules stores at $0293 and $0294 for AdvanceBoundarySequence to play: it counts $0294 down by one each time the player's previous animation has finished, starting the next. Central Park has one: arriving by exit 2 plays kind 1 for 15 steps.
The second byte of each entrance-animation entry, the kind, read with X stepping by three.

The third byte of each entrance-animation entry, its length in animation steps (AdvanceBoundarySequence counts it down once each time the player's previous animation has finished), read with the same X.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide Central Park's reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide Central Park's reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Select Central Park's conditional scene variant and tail-enter the common scene renderer. Inputs: Current area $A2 and persistent flags $03EA for area 1 and $03E9 for area $0D. Outputs: A is the ordinary area number, variant $12, or variant $13; control tail-transfers to the renderer at $8A54. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and all scratch/state clobbered by the tail-called renderer. Hardware: The selector itself changes no I/O; the tail-called renderer updates bitmap, screen, color, and VIC-visible presentation state.

The four items the game expects the player to carry when leaving the level, by their slot in the item flags at $03D8: ResolveLevelCompletion reads them with X from 0 to 3. With all four it leaves at once; while any of their flags is 0 it asks ARE YOU SURE YOU ARE PREPARED FOR THE NEXT LEVEL, and YES leaves anyway. Central Park asks for items 2, 3, 4 and 9.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $C3D7 and $C3CB
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the state changed by InstallAnimation

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $99D4, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($97D7): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos. $9905/$991B/$9931/$9947 use clipped horizontal pixel X to select the destination byte within a three-byte sprite row. Paired with the clearing masks at $99BB; X advances two hires pixels per multicolor source pair.

24 entries: $3F,$3F,$CF,$CF,$F3,$F3,$FC,$FC repeated for three sprite bytes. The scene-condition renderer ANDs these into the selected sprite-row byte whenever the corresponding source pixel pair is nonzero. This removes a two-bit pair, selected jointly with the byte-offset lookup at $99A3. Ends at $99D2; $99D3 is a zero byte between it and the pointer directory, which no instruction reads.

Low-byte base of 20 little-endian condition-list pointers at $99D4-$99FB. $9728 doubles current area to Y; $972A/$972F read paired low/high bytes. Entries 18 and 19 alias lists 1 and 13. There are 18 unique lists; empty lists start with $FF.
High-byte indexed alias for the interleaved directory starting at $99D4; Y is twice the area index. This address is not a separate high-byte array.
Area condition list 0: empty $FF sentinel at $99FC.

Conditionally dispatch the pending script command through the Central Park target-minus-one table
Inputs: command/state bytes $80/$81 and player animation-pointer high byte $61; $80 low six bits select the command; the target-minus-one words start at $A11E and are read from the base $A11C with X = twice the command

RTS completing the stack-built dispatch at $A115. The high-byte indexed load uses this address as its base with X=2*command, so nonzero commands read the high bytes of target-minus-one words beginning at $A11E. 46 little-endian handler-minus-one words at $A11E-$A179. Nonzero command $80&$3F is doubled into X; loads based at $A11C/$A11D build a return address on the stack, then RTS at $A11D enters the selected handler. Word zero corresponds to command 1. Bounds are the table extent before executable handler $A17A; values 47..63 are not represented by this captured table.
