Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E, and compositor and masking scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Compose the Central Park playable phase's player frame $65 into logical actor slot 0, mirrored when the facing flag at $AA21,X ANDed with $1E is non-zero.
Inputs: X is the facing index ($69 shifted right once) into the four mirror flags at $AA21; $1E is the direction bit of $68; $65 is the frame; player position/facing and sprite work buffers are current.
Outputs: Passes $AA21,X AND $1E to ComposeSprites as the mirror flag, with X=0 and Y=$65, composes logical actor slot 0, then falls through to $A4C3, which masks the player's sprites behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, sprite-composition scratch/buffers, and masking scratch.
Hardware: No direct VIC-II register write; the composition helper updates sprite work buffers and changes $01 transiently before restoring it.

Mask the Central Park playable phase's player sprites, actor slot 0, against the area's foreground pictures without recomposing its frame.
Inputs: Player sprite slots 0-3 are composed; $74 supplies the vertical coordinate compared with each foreground record's depth byte; the area's foreground list (pointers at $99D4) is current.
Outputs: Sets X=0, loads A=$74, and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($9720), which clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots' positions, pointers and colours in $0240-$025F.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, and masking scratch; the slots' positions are read from $0200/$0208/$0210.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Rate-limit an update and abort its caller when the slot's minimum interval has not passed. Inputs: X timer slot (2 for the script loop's animation step, 5 for DrawActiveObject, 9 and 10 for the two auxiliary sprite slots, 12 for OpponentAI), global tick $E2, per-slot stamp $0268,X, and threshold table $A4DE. Outputs: the eligible path updates timing state; the ineligible path returns to the caller's caller. Clobbers: A, flags, timing state, and two stack bytes on the abort path.

16 slot-indexed minimum intervals. $A4CD subtracts the slot's last tick $0268,X from current $E2, $A4D0 compares the difference to this table and the gate discards the caller return frame when too soon; accepted calls update the saved tick. Most intervals are 1, with exceptions 6,2 and4 in the captured table; the slots this level uses are 2, 5, 9, 10 and 12, so the 2 at slot 7 is not read.

Translate the normalized Central Park input byte and current player state into facing, movement, pose, action, and animation requests
Inputs: normalized active-high control byte $7C (a set bit is a pressed direction or fire); death/condition latch $B6; player state $61,$65,$68/$69,$6C/$6D,$70,$89; decode tables at $A69C and $A638
Outputs: updates desired direction $68, facing $69, action/motion $6C/$6D, pose $65, dirty flag $9F, and may select/install a player animation
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-control/animation scratch
lda #$00 and sta $02B8: two instructions between an rts and ContinueDirectionalControls that no branch, jump or pointer reaches. The same pair runs at $A569.

Continuation of $A4EE control interpretation: applies desired heading $68, allowing odd headings to replace $69 except an exact opposite; marks redraw $9F when changed. Sets movement $6C and derives facing/pose $65 and $6D. The $A567 idle path clears $02B8 and may select an idle animation; $A591 onward handles changes in the fire/action state $78, comparing direction to facing before selecting an action through $A600. Uses $A638 and $A69C direction lookups; no direct hardware writes. Entry is within the larger control routine, not an independent callable API.

Translate action code A into the Central Park playable phase's player animation pointer and install that animation.
Inputs: A is the action code selected by the control logic (InterpretControls and InterpretNormalizedControls); $69 is player facing; phase animation lookup tables are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $60, derives the facing-adjusted animation index, loads its pointer, initializes $60/$61/$5C/$58/$96/$5D, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $58, $5C/$5D, $60/$61, $6D, and $96.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Install a new player animation-bytecode stream and prime its first control byte
Inputs: X = stream low byte; A = stream high byte; desired direction $68 and facing $69
Outputs: stores the stream pointer in $60/$61, loads its first byte into $5C, clears animation delay $58, copies $68 to $96, and stores $69 bit 1 in $5D
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags; X is preserved

Eight action-heading values 1,7,1,7,5,3,5,3 selected at $A5EE. Index combines desired cardinal direction and current facing, then output replaces desired heading $68 before action animation selection. This is separate from the joystick low-nibble map $A69C.

Interpret the Central Park playable phase's normalized control latch and update player motion/action animation state.
Inputs: $7C is the control byte normalized by ScanAndNormalizeInput ($9418); player animation, action, timing, facing, and collision state are current.
Outputs: Maps the low control nybble through the direction table at $A69C; a new direction, or none, restarts the hold timer $85, sets $88=$FF and sets $6D to the facing halved; once the same direction has been held for the delay from $A694 (4 or 8 ticks) it selects action $84 x 4 + 8 (plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up) through SelectPlayerAnimationForAction, and again at once while the player's mode class is $10. The facing $69 is read, not written.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, player input/action/timing fields ($84, $85, $88, $6D), and animation-installation state on paths that select a new animation.
Hardware: No direct CIA or other hardware-register writes.

Eight alternating delays 4,8 indexed by normalized direction Y. $A66D compares elapsed tick difference against the chosen threshold before deriving action code $84*4+8, plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up, and selecting animation. This table controls action timing, not the joystick direction conversion.

16-entry map of the low four normalized control bits to eight directions 0..7 or $FF for no valid direction. $A507, $A5B5 and $A645 use it to choose movement/facing/action; opposing direction combinations map to $FF. Fire occupies a different input bit and is handled separately.
The player's animations, 36 pointers to their streams in the animation pool, read in pairs by animation number.

High-byte indexed alias of the little-endian pointer/row directory starting at $A6AC. The consumer uses the action code, a multiple of 4, plus 0 or 2 for the facing directly as the byte offset before the paired reads; no separate high-byte allocation begins here. The owning directory describes its full extent.

18 action-mode bases used at $A609: the action code A shifted right twice picks one, and the facing $69 shifted right once is added to it to give the player's action mode $6D, the value the control and combat code compares (as $6D with its low two bits masked) with $10, $0C and $24. The animation pointer at $A6AC is chosen separately, from A itself plus 0 or 2 for the facing. Values include $0C,$04,$18,$10,$1C,$14,$20,$28.

Build, advance, validate, and commit the player's movement candidate for this tick
Inputs: player position $54/$55 and its fractional bytes $50/$51; enemy position $56/$57; desired direction $68; facing $69; elapsed steps $8F; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: initializes candidate $48-$4D and opposing position $C9/$CA, calls AdvanceCandidate, commits candidate position and fractions back to $54/$55,$50/$51, and reports vertical displacement through the shared tail at $A7C9 with X=0
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA

Build and advance the enemy movement candidate, record collision outcomes, and commit it only inside the playable bounds
Inputs: enemy position $56/$57 and its fractional bytes $52/$53; player position $54/$55; desired direction $6A; facing $6B; elapsed steps $8F; profile selector $D3; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: updates candidate/collision scratch; records collision in $02B0/$02B2/$02B4 or failure count $02B1; commits $56/$57,$52/$53 only for X in [$02,$F6] and Y in [$09,$BC]; reports vertical displacement through $A7C9 with X=2
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA,$CD

Add the signed number in A to the actor's $74,X, unless $EF is set or $74,X is 0 or $FF. A positive sum is held at $FF; a negative one is not held at zero but wraps, since the BCS at $A7E8 goes on to the next instruction either way. Inputs: A, and X the actor's offset. Outputs: $74,X. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are kept.

Run the enemy animation interpreter once when the IRQ tick has advanced
Inputs: current tick $E2, enemy animation stamp $026E, and the already-installed enemy animation stream/state at actor offset 2
Outputs: if no tick elapsed, returns unchanged; otherwise stores elapsed delta in $8F, stamps $026E, sets X=2, and tail-enters the shared animation interpreter
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $8F, $026E, and all animation-interpreter scratch/state on the admitted path

Interpret one elapsed step of the selected actor's animation bytecode, including delay, pose, coordinate deltas, event generation, and continuation
Inputs: X=0 at $A802 for player or X=2 at $A804 for enemy; pointer $60/$61,X; control/delay $5C/$58-$59,X; actor position $54/$55,X; elapsed ticks $8F
Outputs: advances delay and stream position, updates pose $65,X, position $54/$55,X, event $64,X, continuation pointer, movement flags, and recomposes the actor's logical sprites when required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and animation, movement, event, collision, and sprite-composition scratch

Run the Central Park playable phase's animation interpreter for the scheduled enemy slot.
Inputs: X is the enemy animation-state offset selected by the scheduler (normally 2); $61,X is its stream pointer high byte; timing and animation state are current.
Outputs: Honors animation delay, decodes one bytecode step when due, updates the enemy animation/movement/event state, composes the resulting actor frame when requested, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02/$03, animation timing/pointer/state bytes for slot X, actor-frame/sprite scratch, and event state selected by the bytecode.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; bytecode paths requesting composition alter sprite work buffers and change CPU-port banking transiently before restoring it.

Compose an actor's current frame and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: X and $4F the actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy) and current animation frame $65,X; the mirror flag is $5D,X when $5C,X bit 4 is set, else $5C,X bit 6; depth $74,X. Outputs: the player is composed into sprite slots 0-3 with ComposeSprites, the enemy into slots 4-7 with ComposeEnemySprites; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery then clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. X is not restored: it returns as 4 for the player and 8 for the enemy. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and shared renderer scratch. Hardware: it writes no chip register itself; the composer it calls switches the I/O area out through the processor port $01 while it reads the packed sprites and puts it back, and MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery stages the slots with interrupts off and ends with CLI.

Return immediately from the Central Park playable phase's animation interpreter on the shared no-further-work path.
Inputs: The preceding animation branch has completed or determined that no frame composition is needed.
Outputs: Returns to the interpreter's caller without additional state or hardware changes.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Delay for the requested number of engine ticks. Inputs: A is the tick count. Outputs: the requested tick transitions have elapsed. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and wait scratch.

Advance an actor candidate by up to eight elapsed substeps and test each proposed segment against compiled collision geometry
Inputs: X = the mover's facing index ($69 or $6B shifted right once, 0-3); Y = movement-profile selector; old/candidate position $48-$4B; candidate fractional bytes $4C/$4D; direction mask $1E; elapsed count $8F
Outputs: stores profile in $027F and capped count in $8E; updates candidate coordinates; returns collision and trigger state through $23/$24,$80/$81,$CD and related movement scratch
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and broad candidate/collision scratch

Four negative-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A90C in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate X, held at 0. Values $70,$C1,$70,$C1.

Four positive-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A926 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is added to the candidate X, held at $FE. Values $07,$1C,$07,$1C.

Four negative-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A940 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $AA19 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate Y. Values $07,$C1,$07,$C1.

Four positive-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A97C in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $AA19 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is added to the candidate Y. Values $70,$1C,$70,$1C.

Four vertical guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A95D and $A999 in AdvanceCandidate after a Y step. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the same Y step is applied twice more, three times in all. All four are $11, directions 0 and 4.

Four horizontal guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $A947 and $A983 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the Y step is skipped. All four are $44, directions 2 and 6.

Four walk-cycle masks, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $A48C in PlayerDriver. Each holds the three directions around that facing: $07 directions 0-2, $1C 2-4, $70 4-6, $C1 6, 7 and 0. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the walk frame (the low three bits of $65) steps forward by one, otherwise back by one.

Four mirror flags, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $A4B7. The flag, ANDed with the direction bit in $1E, is passed to ComposeSprites as its mirror flag $F1, so facing indexes 1 and 3 draw the frame mirrored. Values $00,$FF,$00,$FF.

Consume and dispatch pending player and enemy animation events through the shared target-minus-one event table
Inputs: player event $64 and enemy event $66; event table begins at $AA4B; X=0 selects player and X=2 enemy
Outputs: dispatches each nonzero event through the RTS table, clears $64 after the player handler and $66 after the enemy handler, and returns after both channels are empty
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, two stack bytes per dispatch, and handler-dependent state

Dispatch an event handler through a target-minus-one RTS table. Inputs: A is the event index. Outputs: control transfers to the selected handler, which returns to the original caller. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and two transient stack bytes.

24 little-endian event-handler-minus-one words at $AA4B-$AA7A. $AA40 doubles the event, pushes high then low, and RTS dispatches to word+1. Several slots select $AA7C, and zero selects the no-op $AA7B, although the outer dispatcher skips zero events. Both player and enemy channels use this table.
Odd-byte indexed base of the event directory at $AA4B, read at $AA42 with Y=2*event. This byte is the high byte of slot zero; the directory has 24 words, not a separate high-byte array.

Consume an event-table slot without performing an action.
Inputs: Actor selector X and event index are ignored.
Outputs: Returns immediately; the outer dispatcher subsequently clears the consumed event byte.
Clobbers: No registers or flags; RTS consumes the dispatcher-supplied return address.

If command bit 0 is armed and the player's mode class ($6D with its low two bits masked) is not $0C, move player X by -4, increment player Y and depth, and mark redraw state.
Inputs: Command flags $81, player X/Y $54/$55, depth $74, and player mode $6D; the X supplied by event dispatch is overwritten, so either channel's event moves the player.
Outputs: Eligible path adds signed -4 to $54, increments $55, adds 1 to $74 through ApplySignedActorHeightDelta ($A7C9, with A=1/X=0), and writes $9F=$FF; rejected paths return unchanged.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $54, $55, $74, and $9F.

If command bit 0 is armed and the player's mode class ($6D with its low two bits masked) is not $0C, move player X by +4, increment player Y and depth, and mark redraw state.
Inputs: Command flags $81, player X/Y $54/$55, depth $74, and player mode $6D; the X supplied by event dispatch is overwritten, so either channel's event moves the player.
Outputs: Eligible path adds signed 4 to $54, increments $55, adds 1 to $74 through ApplySignedActorHeightDelta ($A7C9, with A=1/X=0), and writes $9F=$FF; rejected paths return unchanged.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $54, $55, $74, and $9F.

Copy state byte $89 into actor-state byte $70 for two event codes.
Inputs: $89.
Outputs: Writes $70=$89 and returns with A equal to the copied value.
Clobbers: A and flags; $70.

Handle event 3 differently for the player channel and opponent channel.
Inputs: Actor selector X from event dispatch and current animation/AI state.
Outputs: For X=0, waits 20 engine ticks through WaitEngineTicks ($A8F1, A=$14), resets the tick baselines through $11F1, and sets $B4=$FF; for X!=0, sets opponent AI state $CF=$0B.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, animation/pacing scratch, and either $B4 or $CF.

Apply $2C units of player damage for event $0D.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and existing death state.
Outputs: Tail-calls DamagePlayer with A=$2C.
Clobbers: A, flags, player energy $0229, death latch $B6, and combat scratch.

Randomly perturb three paired level-data coordinates, move the opponent two units toward the player on each axis, and damage the player on close overlap.
Inputs: Random source $B51F, coordinate pairs at $CE49/$CE4A for X offsets 8/4/0, player position $54/$55, and opponent position $56/$57.
Outputs: Keeps each data perturbation inside its encoded eight-value range, adjusts $56/$57 by two toward $54/$55, and calls player damage with A=1 when absolute X<8 and absolute Y<10.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, scratch $1E, $CE49/$CE4A records, opponent coordinates $56/$57, and possibly player energy/death state.

Run object mode 3 for the player, then test the combat overlap and apply the actor-to-actor hit, damage, score, and reaction result
Inputs: X = attacking actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy); this entry sets Y=3, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (TestActorCombatOverlap then overwrites Y); actor geometry/state; action modes $6D/$6F; damage tables $ABA6/$ABBA
Outputs: on overlap, ignores a target already in reaction $24, otherwise selects damage, calls DamagePlayer or DamageEnemy, awards score through $1187 when the player is the attacker, and latches the opposing actor's reaction
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, overlap/damage/score scratch, and object-engine state on the player channel

Resolve the selected combat-contact event. Inputs: actor state and the contact type selected by the entry path. Outputs: damage, reaction animation, collision, and object state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and combat scratch. Hardware: may change presentation or audio indirectly through damage and animation helpers.

Run object mode 5 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $AD46-$AD85.
Outputs: Loads Y=5, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Run object mode 6 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X (the attacker), both actors' positions/headings/animation modes, energy fields, and collision profile tables $AD46-$AD85.
Outputs: Loads Y=6, which ObjectEngine takes as its object mode when X is 0 (the overlap test then overwrites Y); runs the shared overlap query, whose combat index comes from the attacker's mode $6D,X and state $70,X; on a hit applies damage to the opposing actor plus the corresponding reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, object-engine state, and possible death/defeat persistence.

Resolve the Central Park playable phase's combat overlap for attacking actor slot X, selecting the player or opponent damage and reaction path.
Inputs: X selects the attacker, actor slot 0 or the opponent slot 2; Y is the object mode for ObjectEngine; actor positions and combat state are current.
Outputs: When X is 0, runs ObjectEngine ($BFC3) with Y as the object mode and sets X=0 again; then runs the overlap test itself at $AB70 (TestActorCombatOverlap) and, on a hit, applies the matching hit/reaction/damage logic and updates actor/combat state. It returns no meaningful result.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, combat/reaction scratch, object-engine state, and the affected actor's health/action state.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Resolve combat overlap using the profile derived from the selected actor's current mode, then dispatch damage and reaction.
Inputs: Actor selector X plus both actors' positions, headings, animation modes, energies, and collision profile tables.
Outputs: Runs $AC7A to derive the active profile and overlap result; on a hit applies actor-specific damage and reaction animation.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F/$C5/$C6, actor animation/combat state, energy, and possible death/defeat persistence.

20 attack strengths read at $AB88 for an enemy attack against the player; each is the energy DamagePlayer subtracts. Index $1F is the enemy's attack mode $6F minus $14 shifted right twice (0-3, since its attack modes are $14-$23), ORed with its profile $72 times 4 (a profile of 4 and up counts as 0), so only entries 0-15 can be read; the result enters the saturating player-damage routine $B54A. The last four bytes ($ABB6-$ABB9) are not reached by this index.

16 attack values read at $AB91/$AB97 for player attacks, passed both to score accounting $1187 and the enemy-damage routine DamageEnemy ($B568). That routine subtracts the value from the enemy's energy $022A, held at 0: it is conventional energy subtraction, and the IRQ only moves the displayed meter $022B,X toward the energy.

Select and install the victim's hit-reaction animation. Inputs: X the victim's offset (0 player, 2 enemy); the victim's facing $69,X, mode $6D,X and energy, and the attacker's mode. Outputs: unless the victim's mode class is already $24, $6D,X is saved in $71,X and set to the facing halved plus $24. If the victim still has energy, a reaction pointer from the table at $AC3A, chosen by the attacker's mode and the victim's facing, is installed: for the player through InstallAnimation, with $02BD cleared, and for the enemy through InstallAiScript. If the victim's energy is 0, the player gets no new animation and $02BD is cleared, and the enemy gets the defeat script $C3D7 or $C3CB (by $6B bit 2) through InstallAiScript, with $CF=7 and $0236=0. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state.

32 little-endian animation/script pointers at $AC3A-$AC79. $AC01/$AC10 and their paired high reads select one using the attacker's mode and the victim's facing; $AC01 (player victim) installs it through InstallAnimation ($A61F) and $AC10 (enemy victim) through InstallAiScript ($AD3B). Targets are streams in the $C2C4-$C4C1 pool; table stores absolute pointers, unlike the event RTS directory.
High-byte base of the interleaved pointer table $AC3A, read with even Y by $AC04/$AC13. The physical table holds 32 two-byte entries through $AC79.

Test whether the selected combat actors overlap. Inputs: X selects an actor and current positions and bounds are valid. Outputs: flags and transient contact state report overlap or separation. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and overlap scratch.

Mark AI scripting active and install a new AI script pointer. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $76 is set to one, $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Install an AI script without changing the active marker. Inputs: X is pointer low and A is pointer high. Outputs: $62/$63 receive the pointer, $5E/$5A are cleared, A returns zero, and X is preserved. Clobbers: A, N, Z, and AI script state; X and Y are preserved.

Finish installing a Central Park AI script when its low pointer byte was stored separately. Inputs: A is the script-pointer high byte and $62 already contains its low byte. Outputs: $63 receives A, $5E and $5A are cleared, and A returns zero; $62 is unchanged. Clobbers: A, N, Z, $63, $5E, and $5A; X, Y, C, V, and $62 are preserved.

16 unsigned lower horizontal bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper horizontal bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 unsigned lower vertical bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

16 exclusive upper vertical bounds. $ACAE-$AD12 derives index from attack-pose class and selected object/weapon state, then compares separation with these paired limits. $FF slots remain literal bounds; their ordinary-play reachability is open. These are combat-overlap parameters, not graphics.

Restore an actor's saved mode, derive its facing/pose code, and perform channel-specific follow-up.
Inputs: Actor channel offset X, current heading/mode at $69+X, saved mode at $71+X, and actor state arrays $5D/$65.
Outputs: Copies heading bit 1 to $5D+X, restores $6D+X from $71+X, derives $65+X from restored/current heading; player channel sets $9F=$FF, opponent channel rebuilds state and sets $CF=8.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, $5D+X/$6D+X/$65+X, and either $9F or opponent helper/AI state.

Admit and dispatch one active-opponent AI step, or route collision/boundary state to recovery
Inputs: active-enemy sign latch $CB; collision/boundary fields $02B0-$02B2; AI state $CF; timer slot 12; target-minus-one table beginning at $ADEA
Outputs: inactive enemies return; collision/boundary state jumps to recovery at $B11E; admitted normal state dispatches the selected AI handler by stack/RTS
Clobbers: A, X, flags, two stack bytes, and handler-dependent state; Y is preserved until the handler
16 target-minus-one words $ADEA-$AE09 selected by twice AI state $CF. $ADDE/$ADE2 push high/low and RTS transfers to word+1. Slot 14 stores $FFFF and would wrap to zero, which would return to $0000.
High-byte indexed alias of the 16-word AI RTS directory at $ADEA; even X comes from twice $CF. Keep the $FFFF slot visible as an unresolved state case.

Set the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 4 plus its facing $6B shifted right once; this is AI state 0's handler in the table at $ADEA.
Inputs: Current opponent facing $6B.
Outputs: Stores floor(($6B + 8)/2), which is 4 + $6B/2, in $6F and returns.
Clobbers: A and flags; $6F.

Set the Central Park opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus its facing through the common tail at $AE10.
Inputs: $6B is the current opponent facing/direction code.
Outputs: Computes $6F=(2*0+$6B)/2, mode class 0 plus the facing halved, and returns with it stored in $6F.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, and $6F; X and Y are preserved.

Set the opponent's action mode. Inputs: A is the mode class (0, 4, 8, an attack class $14-$20, or $24 for defeat) and $6B is the opponent's facing. Outputs: $6F = A + $6B/2, the class plus the facing halved, the same layout as the player's $6D. Clobbers: A, flags, and $6F.

Initialize a timed AI decision state and its random delay.
Inputs: AI option byte $D0 bit 6, tick $E2, current heading $6B, and random source $B51F.
Outputs: Sets state $CF to 3 or 4, snapshots tick to $0275, stores random delay 0..31 in $CC, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0275, $CC, $6F, and random-source scratch.

Wait for the AI delay to expire, then enter state 5 with a rebuilt heading/action.
Inputs: Current tick $E2, delay origin $0275, delay $CC, current heading $6B, and helper state.
Outputs: Before expiry returns unchanged; at expiry sets $CF=5, derives and stores a new heading in $6A/$6B, invokes setup $B346 with X=8, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Face the opponent into the player's current relative quadrant and enter approach state 5.
Inputs: Player high-byte coordinates $54/$55 and opponent high-byte coordinates $56/$57; opponent heading and action fields.
Outputs: Sets AI state $CF=5, stores the quadrant classification returned by $B32E into both $6B (current heading) and $6A (desired heading), installs direction action class 8 through $B346 with X=8, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved through $AE10, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $6A/$6B/$6F/$CF and helper scratch.

After the timed delay, choose a two-step heading turn, enter state 2, and begin horizontal-travel tracking.
Inputs: Tick/delay fields $E2/$0275/$CC, random source, heading $6B, and opponent X $56.
Outputs: At expiry sets $CF=2, rotates $6A/$6B by +2 or -2 modulo 8, snapshots $56 in $D1, runs setup X=$18, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved, then continues into the travel tracker at $AE81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, $D1, and helper scratch.

Track horizontal displacement from $D1, escalate after at least $14 units, and fall back to state 5 when the range test drops below $70.
Inputs: Opponent heading $6B, current X $56, baseline X $D1, tick $E2, and distance helper $B30C.
Outputs: At sufficient directed displacement sets $CF=$0C, snapshots tick, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved; independently, a helper result below $70 resets through the state-5 entry at $AE3A, which sets $CF=5 and turns $6A/$6B toward the player.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $0275, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Twelve ticks after state $0C began, enter state $0F, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state $0F has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275, heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 12 ticks returns; afterward updates $0275, sets $CF=$0F, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0275, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Six ticks after state $0F began, enter state 2, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state 2 has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275 (written when state $0F began, and not updated here), heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 6 ticks returns; afterward sets $CF=2, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=$18, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Steer the enemy toward the player. Inputs: the player's position ($54/$55) and joystick heading $68, the enemy's position ($56/$57) and heading $6B, its profile $72 and behaviour $CB, the positions kept in $028A/$028B and $028E/$028F, and the tick $E2. It aims at a point level with the player, as far to one side as the profile's entry in $B2FD says, on the side the enemy is on, judged against the player's X less 8 when $68 is 0 to 3, plus 8 when it is 4 to 7, or unchanged when $68 is negative. When that point is less than 6 away from the enemy (Manhattan distance), or when the point would fall off the screen, it goes to RetargetAiToPlayer ($AF42): that keeps the player's position in $028A/$028B, faces the enemy toward the player and enters state 6. It also holds the enemy's X between 4 and $F7, retargeting when it has to. With $CB at $80 and the player 56 or more away, it enters state 9 when the player is at least as far from the position in $028E/$028F as the enemy is (half the X distance plus half the Y distance each), and keeps the player's position there. Otherwise, when the heading toward the point and the heading toward the player differ in bit 2, it retargets one time in 16 (a random byte below $10) if the player is less than 8 away vertically. Then it turns the enemy toward the point (a turn that changes bit 2 of the heading waits until 20 ticks have passed since the last, kept in $02BE) and sets the heading $6A from the table at $B304: the entry before $6B when a quarter of the horizontal distance to the point is less than the vertical one, the entry for $6B when the vertical distance is under 4, and $6B itself otherwise. Outputs: $6A, $6B, $6F, $CF and the enemy's action. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1C-$21, $56, $028A/$028B, $028E/$028F, $02BE and the random-number state $F9-$FB.

Retarget the Central Park playable phase's opponent AI to the player's current coordinates.
Inputs: Player coordinates are $54/$55 and the enemy's are $56/$57.
Outputs: Copies $54/$55 to $028A/$028B, sets $6A/$6B to the diagonal heading from the enemy toward the player (ClassifyRelativeActorQuadrant), installs that heading's action from the table at $B376 (InstallAiActionByDirection with X=4), sets $6F to mode class 0 plus the heading (the heading shifted right once), sets $CF=6, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, $1F, the enemy's animation fields $5A/$5B/$5E/$5F/$62/$63, $028A/$028B, $6A/$6B/$6F, and $CF.
Hardware: No hardware registers are read or written.

Choose between an immediate recovery/timer state and a randomized attack setup from the player's current actor mode.
Inputs: Player actor mode $6D, behavior selector $72, tick $E2, random source, opponent heading $6B, and AI sequence counter $02BD.
Outputs: If ($6D&$FC)==$24, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5; otherwise selects a bounded random action/setup, sets $CF=7, and increments $02BD.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0 on the attack path), flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, $6F, $02BD, the random-number state $F9-$FB, and helper scratch.

Choose and install a random close-range opponent action for the Central Park playable phase.
Inputs: Opponent/player proximity tests have reached the close-range branch; the enemy's profile $72 (zero allows two variants, nonzero four), its heading $6B, animation state, and PRNG are current.
Outputs: Selects a bounded random variant, installs its animation/heading parameters through the phase helpers, sets $CF=7, increments $02BD, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, PRNG state $F9-$FB, helper scratch, action/animation state, $CF, and $02BD.
Hardware: No hardware registers are written; each PRNG call reads CIA 1 Timer A low at $DC04 and reads high at $DC05 only on reseeding.

Wait for the opponent animation pointer high byte to clear, then initialize AI state 8 timing.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63, tick $E2, and random source.
Outputs: Returns while $63 is nonzero; when zero, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, and random-source scratch.

Decide whether the player is close enough to the AI target for a scripted action. Inputs: player coordinates, $028A/$028B target coordinates, and AI state and timers. Outputs: proximity and action state are updated and an AI path may be entered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI scratch.

Wait for both opponent animation completion and projectile slot 1 inactivity, then reset through AI state 5.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63 and projectile slot-1 state $0281.
Outputs: Returns if either field is nonzero; when both are zero, tail-enters the state-5 reset at $AE3A.
Clobbers: A, flags, and on reset A/X/Y (Y left 0) plus $CF/$6A/$6B/$6F, $1F, the enemy's animation fields and helper scratch.

Return at once, for state 10, the one enemy state that does nothing (its word in the dispatch table at $ADEA is $B0C8). Its RTS returns to the code that called OpponentAI: the address the dispatcher pushed at $ADDE-$ADE5 was used up by the RTS at $ADE6 that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Let a defeated enemy get up again once its energy has refilled (AI state 11, which SpawnEnemy sets for an enemy restored as defeated).
Inputs: Area index $A2, the area's defeat byte $012D,X, the ticks $E2/$F0 and the defeat time $0175,X/$0187,X, player/opponent positions $54-$57, heading $6B, and animation pointers $C3ED/$C3E3.
Outputs: Returns at once while $012D,X is $FF (beaten for good). Otherwise rebuilds the enemy's energy from the ticks since its defeat (RebuildEnemyMeterFromElapsedTicks, which writes $022A and $3F92,X); when that has reached 44 and the player is not within 12 horizontally and 6 vertically, clears bit 7 of $012D,X, sets $CF=7, installs the animation at $C3ED (heading bit 2 clear) or $C3E3 (bit 2 set) through InstallAiScript ($AD3B), and writes $0236=6; otherwise returns without transition.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F, $022A, $3F92,X, and when the enemy gets up $012D,X, $CF, enemy animation state $5A/$5E/$62/$63, and $0236.
A second rts after the one at $B11C, never reached.

Handle what the enemy's last move ran into.
Inputs: $02B0 is the offset of the compiled collision record the enemy's move hit (stored by MoveEnemy at $A78A) or $FF; $02B1 counts moves that left the play area and $02B2 other blocked moves; $02B3 is the record being followed and $02A4/$02A5 the last two records hit.
Outputs: Reads $02B0 and sets it to $FF. With a record: unless it is already $02B3 it becomes $02B3, is pushed into $02A4 (the old $02A4 into $02A5) when it is not $02A4, and ChooseEnemyFacingFromContactState picks the heading, with A=2 when it equals the old $02A5 and A=0 otherwise. Then a nonzero $02B1 clears $02B1/$02B2, sets $02B3=$FF and enters state 5 (AiFacePlayerQuadrant); a nonzero $02B2 clears it, sets $02B3=$FF and retargets ($AF42); otherwise it enters state $0D, clears both and runs AiTrackSelectedCollisionRecord. With $FF: when the player is less than 14 away (Manhattan) it clears $02B1/$02B2, sets $02B3=$FF and either sets $CF=5 with action mode 8 (horizontal distance under 12) or retargets; otherwise it enters state 5 when $02B1 is nonzero, or retargets.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $1C/$1D, $02B0-$02B3, $02A4/$02A5, $CF, and AI action/heading state on every path.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Follow the collision record the enemy ran into (AI state $0D) and give it up when the enemy has passed it or the player comes near.
Inputs: Selected record offset $02B3 ($FF for none), the record's start and end X at $FEF9,X/$FEFB,X, opponent position $56/$57, player position $54/$55, current heading $6B, the side bit $02B5, and the tick $E2.
Outputs: Sets $02B3 to $FF and enters state 5 (AiFacePlayerQuadrant) when there is no record or the enemy's X is 8 or more below the record's start X or 4 or more above its end X; sets $02B3 to $FF and retargets at $AF42 when the player is less than 14 away (Manhattan distance); sets $02B3 to $FF, keeps $E2 in $02BE and enters state 5 when the enemy is heading straight away from the player, 8 or more away horizontally, and the player's vertical side matches $02B5; otherwise returns with nothing changed.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02B3, $02BE, $1C/$1D, $1F, $6A/$6B, $6F, $CF, and helper scratch.

Choose enemy facing and action from contact geometry. Inputs: A is 0 or 2 (2 when the record just hit is the one hit before the last), X is the previously followed record offset or $FF, and the enemy's heading $6B, the actor positions, the side bits $02B4/$02B5 and the record's byte 4 at $FEFD,$02B3 are valid. Outputs: $6A/$6B are set from the table at $B2BD (reversed when X is not $FF and $02B4 differs from $02B5), the action is reinstalled when the heading changed, action mode 8 is set, $02B5 takes $02B4, and for a record whose byte 4 AND $3E is 5 or more $6A is replaced from $B2AD; a negative table entry hangs in a loop that increments the border colour. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F, and AI state.

16 direction-selection bytes read at $B29F, for a record whose byte 4 AND $3E is 5 or more. The index is half the enemy's heading $6B, then bit 0 of $02B4, then whether the record's bit 6 ($40) is set, shifted in in that order. Nonnegative result becomes desired heading $6A; a negative entry takes the trap loop at $B2A7, which increments the border colour $D020 for ever.

64 contact-geometry direction entries, $B2BD-$B2FC. $B24F combines flags and selector state into Y, then $B252 loads this table; negative entries take the trap, otherwise heading may be reversed and stored in $6A/$6B. A direction map for collision/AI decisions, not sprite selectors.

Seven distance offsets read at $AF2A/$AF34 using the enemy profile $72. Added to or subtracted from player X to decide opponent approach. The following heading-map base starts at $B304; profile bounds outside these seven values are not assumed.

Eight headings, read at $B02E once the distances to the target are in $1C and $1D ($B30E). When a quarter of $1C is less than $1D the entry read is the one before the enemy's heading $6B (the SBC #$00 at $B02B runs with the carry clear); $6B is always odd where it is set, so that is entry 0, 2, 4 or 6, a vertical heading. Otherwise, when $1D is less than 4, it is the entry for $6B itself, a horizontal heading. The entry becomes the enemy's new heading $6A, which is $6B unchanged when neither holds. The table ends at $B30B, before the Manhattan-distance routine.

Compute Manhattan distance between the engine's two coordinate pairs. Inputs: $54/$55 and $56/$57 are the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved.

Compute saturated Manhattan distance with the first X coordinate supplied by the caller. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: $1C and $1D receive the absolute horizontal and vertical deltas; A is their sum saturated at $FF. Clobbers: A, flags, $1C, and $1D; X and Y are preserved.

Classify the first coordinate pair's quadrant relative to the second: the diagonal heading from the second pair ($56/$57, the enemy) toward the first ($54/$55, the player). Inputs: $54-$57 contain the two coordinate pairs. Outputs: A is the heading 7, 5, 1 or 3 from the table at $B342 (index bit 1 set when the first X is not less than the second, bit 0 when the first Y is not less than the second), X is that index, and $1F has the X comparison's carry shifted into bit 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved.

Classify relative quadrant with the first X coordinate supplied in A. Inputs: A is first X and $55-$57 hold the remaining coordinates. Outputs: A is the phase-table quadrant/direction code and $1F contains transient horizontal comparison state. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and $1F; Y is preserved.
The four diagonal headings 7, 5, 1 and 3: ClassifyQuadrantFromPresetX makes a number from 0 to 3 from two comparisons of X and Y positions and returns the heading it picks here.

Select and install the AI action matching the enemy's heading and an action class. Inputs: X is the action-table offset (the class); the heading is read from $6B (A is not an input), and $D3 picks the frame delay. Outputs: X is moved on by 2 when $6B is 1 or 7; $5F = $6B AND 2, $5B = the delay from $B372, $62/$63 = the pointer from $B376,X, $5E = the stream's first byte and $5A = 0. Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), flags, and AI script state.

Four action delays 8,6,4,4 indexed by $D3 at $B358 and written to $5B, the enemy animation's frame delay (the interpreter copies it into the countdown $5A at each command that brings no delay of its own), before an AI action is installed.

26 little-endian action/animation pointers through $B3A9. $B346 derives an even table offset from facing/action class, reads low/high via $B376/$B377 and installs $62/$63 with its first opcode at $5E. Targets include the main $C2C4 animation pool and four small retained streams beginning $B3AA.
High-byte indexed base of the action pointer table beginning $B376; X is an even offset. The table ends before retained action-stream bytes at $B3AA.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3AA-$B3AD. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3AE-$B3B1. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3B2-$B3C3. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Action stream selected by the $B376 directory, $B3C4-$B3D5. Commands use the animation header/frame/optional-event/continuation format: bit 5 ends a sequence with a word pointer, zero stops. The long streams advance frames 8..15 and 0..7 respectively and loop to their own entries; short streams stop after one frame.

Rebuild the current area enemy meter from the 16-bit tick pair $F0:$E2 and saved tick origin $0187,X:$0175,X. Computes delta modulo 65536, shifts right five, subtracts two with a zero floor and clamps to 44. Writes both $022A and $3F92,X. The inputs are elapsed ticks, not world-height coordinates; X is current area $A2.

Draw a phase-local UI or status image record. Inputs: A is image index and X is placement variant. Outputs: the selected UI image is rendered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02-$05, and renderer scratch. Hardware: reads VIC-II control state at $D011 and changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

The scene list that $B434-$B43A points $02/$03 at before jumping to RenderUiSceneRecord, which takes the image from $04/$05 and its place from $25 and $26. Its one record, $00 $0E $0E, has bits 5 and 6 of its third byte clear, so no colour pairs follow (read at $8B80) and AdvanceSceneRecordPointer steps three bytes on, to the $FF at $B447 that ends the list at $8A9A.
Rows 3 and 9, one for each of the panel's two item boxes: DrawUiImageRecord reads the row for the box in X here and draws the item's picture at column 33 of it.

Crumble the sprites away, then clear them: 769 passes, each ANDing one random mask from $B51B into one random byte (0 to 63) of all 16 sprite buffers at $0C00-$0FFF, the two sets of the eight slots' images, with a short wait after each; then it clears all 1,024 bytes. The sprites on screen change because their images do. Inputs: the random-number state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E-$21 and the random-number state.

The masks $3F, $CF, $F3 and $FC, each clearing one of the four two-bit pixels of a multicolour byte. Each pass of DissolveSpriteImages ($B456) picks one random offset from 0 to 63 and one of these masks at random, and ANDs that mask into the byte at that offset in all 16 sprite buffers at $0C00-$0FFF, so the sprites crumble a pixel at a time.

Advance and return Central Park's table- and CIA-timer-mixed pseudo-random byte. Inputs: $F9/$FA is the readable table pointer, $FB is the previous random byte, Y is caller state to preserve, and CIA 1 Timer A is running at $DC04/$DC05. Outputs: If old $FA is at least $CE, sets $FA=($DC04 & $1F)+$8A and $F9=$DC05. Then A and $FB receive old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] + $DC04 modulo 256, plus 1 when old $FB + byte[$F9/$FA] passes 255 (the second ADC keeps that carry); $F9 increments and $FA increments on low-byte wrap; Y is restored. Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, V, and $F9-$FB; X and Y are preserved. Hardware: Reads CIA 1 Timer A low byte $DC04 on every call and high byte $DC05 only on reseed; performs no hardware write.

Subtract unsigned A from player health $0229 with saturation at zero. Positive remaining health preserves action $6D and death latch $B6. Only the zero-result path sets $6D=($69>>1)+$24 and $B6=$FF. X/Y are preserved; no hardware registers are written.

Subtract the damage in A from the enemy's energy, keep the area's copy of it, and on defeat persist position/time state and award score
Inputs: A = unsigned damage; enemy health $022A; current area $A2; enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B; tick/time state; defeated-count limit $D6
Outputs: stores the energy, held at 0, in $022A and in the area's copy at $3F92,$A2, which the area gets back when the player returns; on defeat awards score, records position/heading/time in $013F/$0151/$0163/$0175/$0187 indexed by area, advances bounded persistent state $012D,X, and installs reaction/action $24
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and score/persistence/reaction scratch

Create the current area's enemy from static spawn tables or restore its persistent defeated/position record
Inputs: area index $A2; spawn/profile tables $B67F,$B691,$B6A3,$B6B5,$B6C7; persistent state $012D/$013F/$0151/$0163; related enemy profile fields
Outputs: initializes enemy script/motion, extents, delay, AI state, type/attributes, position, heading, action and timing fields; a zero spawn Y disables the enemy; otherwise composes its initial logical sprites
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and enemy/script/sprite-composition state

Eight pose entries read at $B64A. Y is half the selected enemy heading on the ordinary path and an adjusted heading on the preserved-enemy path; result goes to $67. The table is separate from the area-indexed enemy fields.
Eight mirror/auxiliary flags read at $B64F using the same heading-derived Y as $B66F; writes $5F. Values are zero or $FF.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B67F-$B690: upper nibble selects $7F, lower nibble $72; lower nibble with bit 7 sets $CB. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B691-$B6A2: initial enemy X written to $56. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6A3-$B6B4: initial enemy Y written to $57/$76; zero takes the no-spawn path. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6B5-$B6C6: low three bits set heading $6B; upper nibble sets $D6. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

18 area-indexed enemy spawn entries at $B6C7-$B6D8: sets $D0, with low two bits copied to $D3. Consumers are $B5DF-$B659; preserved coordinates may override initial X/Y. Values are loaded from the captured Central Park level.

Spawn the attacking actor's projectile into its fixed player or enemy slot after the combat-overlap precheck
Inputs: X = source actor offset (0 player, nonzero enemy); actor position/facing $54-$57/$69/$6B; player selected-object state $70/$0279/$03DC; projectile arrays $0280-$0289
Outputs: player attacks populate slot 0 only when free and allowed by selected-object state; enemy attacks populate slot 1; position, direction, lifetime, and collision stamps are initialized
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and combat-overlap/projectile initialization scratch

Launch the enemy's projectile into slot 1 when that slot is free. Inputs: A is the projectile kind; the enemy's position $56/$57 and heading $6B. Outputs: when $0281 is free, sets the lifetime $0289 to $FF, the kind $0281 to A, the heading $0283 to $6B, the start $0285/$0287 to the enemy's position plus the heading's offsets from $B927/$B928, and $0296 to $FF; when the X offset carries the start off either side of the play area the kind is cleared to 0 and nothing is launched; when the slot is occupied nothing changes. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and projectile state; Y is kept.

Test a projectile/actor pair against the engine's two-axis collision box. Inputs: X selects projectile coordinates $0284,X/$0286,X; Y selects actor coordinates $54,Y/$55,Y. Outputs: carry is clear exactly when absolute vertical distance is below 8 and absolute horizontal distance is below 6; carry is set on either rejection. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are preserved.

Launch the player's projectile, in slot 0: A is its lifetime, which UpdateProjectiles counts down ($0288), and X its kind ($0280). It starts at the player's position ($54, $55) plus the offsets for the player's heading $69 from $B927 and $B928 ($0284, $0286), flies on that heading ($0282), and $0295 is set to $FF. When the X offset carries the start off either side of the play area, the kind is cleared to 0 and nothing is launched. Clobbers: A, X and flags; Y is kept.

Move the two projectile slots on by the ticks since the last call ($E2 less $0273, kept in $8F), slot 1 then slot 0, and return at once when none has passed. Each tick counts down a projectile's lifetime ($0288,X), and it is removed when that runs out. While the lifetime is 8 or more it also moves a step on its heading (the X and Y steps at $B92F and $B930), and it is removed when its X leaves 0-$FC or its Y leaves $22-$B0, or, for kinds 0 and 1, when the scenery in front has masked its sprite to nothing (bytes 1, 4 and 7 of the sprite at $0CC0 or $0EC0 for slot 0, $0DC0 or $0FC0 for slot 1, as $0295 or $0296 is 0 or not, all zero; nothing is tested while it is negative). Then a projectile of kind 0 to 5 is tested against the other side's actor (TestProjectileCollisionBox, $B767), unless that actor's action ($6D or $6F, the low two bits aside) is $24 or $0C: slot 1's hits the player, who loses 22 of energy (DamagePlayer, $B54A), and slot 0's, the player's, hits the enemy while $CB is negative, which loses 44, a full bar (DamageEnemy, $B568). A hit starts the actor's reaction ($ABCA) and removes the projectile. Kinds 6 and 7 hit nothing. Removing a projectile clears its kind ($0280,X) and its sprite's entries at $0213 and $024B for slot 0, $0217 and $024F for slot 1. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E and $8F.

Projectile-state indexed graphic field, read at $BCE6/$BCEF. When the paired high byte at $B8FA is nonzero, this is the low byte of the address of a raw, unpacked 63-byte image ($FBE0, or $FC20 in the other phase, for kinds 2 to 5), which is blitted straight from $06/$07. With the high byte zero, this byte is a packed-sprite number passed to $BF1E. The EOR #$08 at $BCD3 toggles bit 3 of the state before each lookup, so entries 0-7 and 8-15 alternate as the projectile's two image phases.

Indexed high byte paired with $B8EA: nonzero uses a direct source pointer; zero chooses the packed-sprite directory through the low field. Entries with $FB/$FC point into the retained raw/high graphics bank. Ordinary projectile-state bounds remain a separate verification question.

Projectile-state indexed logical-sprite attribute byte read at $BCD9 and stored to $0220,X. $FF and values 1/6 are retained literally. It supplies display attributes; the adjacent offset maps at $B919/$B920 serve position adjustment instead.

Projectile kind-indexed X offsets for its sprite. $BD0B masks the projectile's kind ($0280,Y) to three bits, adds this byte to the projectile's X and writes the staged logical-sprite X. Seven bytes; kind 7 reads $B920, the first byte of the Y table.

Projectile kind-indexed Y offsets for its sprite. $BD0B masks the projectile's kind ($0280,Y) to three bits, adds this byte to the projectile's Y and writes the staged logical-sprite Y. Seven bytes; kind 7 reads $B927, the first byte of the spawn table.

Indexed X-offset base read at $B742/$B794 using actor heading X. Added to enemy/player X with explicit overflow rejection before storing projectile X. Paired Y-offset reads use the overlapping base $B928, so these bases must not be described as disjoint eight-byte arrays.
Indexed Y spawn-offset base at $B758/$B7AA, read using actor heading X and added to enemy/player Y. Overlaps the X-offset base $B927. This is spawn positioning, not a movement increment lookup.

X movement-increment base read at $B844. Y combines projectile heading and a projectile-kind offset from $B948; negative X increments take a borrow-check path, while positive increments take a carry-check path before writing $0284,X. The neighboring $B930 base supplies Y movement, so the bytes are indexed coordinate pairs rather than a separate eight-byte Y table.
Y movement increments read at $B85E with the same combined index as the $B92F X increments. Adds to $0286,X, then rejects coordinates below $22 or at least $B1. Indexed bases overlap.

Physical continuation bytes in the indexed projectile-motion parameter pool beginning $B92F/$B930. Effective reads are formed by adding heading and kind offset; no instruction directly addresses $B936. This is not a separate spawn-offset table, and its values retain the motion-pool context.

Physical continuation bytes in the indexed projectile-motion parameter pool beginning $B92F/$B930. Effective reads are formed by adding heading and kind offset; no instruction directly addresses $B93D. This is not a separate spawn-offset table, and its values retain the motion-pool context.

Four bytes at the end of the projectile-motion pool that begins at $B92F/$B930: UpdateProjectiles reads them as X and Y steps ($B844, $B85E) for kinds 2 to 5 at the higher headings, where the index (the heading plus the kind's offset from $B948) reaches $14-$1B. Projectile setup does not read them: the spawn offsets at $B927/$B928 end at $B92F.

Eight kind-indexed offsets used at $B7DC. Projectile state is masked with $07; the selected byte is added to heading $0282,X to form the X/Y movement-table index. These bytes select a motion profile; they are not unknown projectile setup parameters.

Expand the current area's encoded collision list into fixed six-byte segment records for movement tests
Inputs: area index $A2; concatenated $FF-terminated source lists beginning at $9D8A; line/slope parameters consumed by the compiler and Multiply
Outputs: emits endpoint, gradient, flags, and optional-action fields as six-byte records beginning at $FEF9 and writes a zero terminator at the next record
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and collision-compiler arithmetic/pointer scratch

Compute an unsigned 8-by-8-bit product for collision arithmetic
Inputs: X = unsigned multiplicand; Y = unsigned multiplier
Outputs: Y:X = 16-bit unsigned product
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $45-$47

Test the candidate movement segment against the compiled collision records until one is crossed, and report the collision plus any encoded trigger
Inputs: X = heading/direction selector; old and candidate coordinates $48-$4B; movement profile $027F; six-byte records beginning at $FEF9
Outputs: returns A=$FF for collision or A=0 for none and restores X from $F3; records the matched record offset in $24 on a collision; when $027F is 0, a crossed segment with bit 0 of its flags set is a trigger: it stores the record's action byte in $80 and counts as a collision only when that byte is negative, and after the scan $81 becomes $81 plus 1 with bit 7 set
Clobbers: A, Y, flags and collision arithmetic scratch including $21-$24,$45-$47,$C5,$F3; X is restored on return

Compose the enemy's frame: the same as ComposeSprites, but with $92 set to $80 plus the enemy's profile $72 (its low two bits pick the frame's weapon part) instead of the player's weapon $70. Inputs: A is the mirror flag (stored in $F1), Y the frame number and X the first logical sprite slot (4, from $A8DA). Outputs: the enemy's parts are drawn into its sprite images and their positions, attributes and flags set. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and extensive compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Decode one actor frame descriptor into positioned logical sprite components, temporarily switching the I/O area out to read the packed sprites in the RAM under $D000-$DFFF
Inputs: A = frame attribute/modifier; Y = frame-descriptor index; X = first logical-sprite slot; actor state including $70,$7D and frame pointer tables at $C4C2
Outputs: draws the parts into the slots' sprite images ($0C00-$0FFF) and writes their positions, attributes, flags, and ready state into logical sprite arrays $0200-$0258, setting sprite-dirty state as required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and sprite-composition scratch including $F1,$92,$9F
Hardware: decrements then restores CPU port $01 to switch the I/O area out transiently; does not directly write VIC-II sprite registers
sta $F1, never reached: ComposeSprites makes the same store at $BBC0 and jumps over these two bytes to $BBD5.

Enter the Central Park playable phase's common sprite-composition body with the mode already prepared by ComposeSprites ($BBC0, $92 from the player's weapon $70) or by the enemy's entry at $BBB5 ($92 set to $80 plus $72).
Inputs: $F1 is the mirror flag, set when the actor faces the other way, and the low two bits of $92 pick one of a six-part frame's three alternatives; X selects the logical sprite group; Y selects the frame descriptor; CPU port $01 is in the engine's normal I/O-visible state.
Outputs: Decrements $01 for the required high-memory RAM visibility, resolves and composes the selected frame into logical sprite work buffers and the slots' sprite images, restores $01 before return, and records composition state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $02-$07, $1E, $42-$44, $97, $C5-$C7, $0237, $F1 on the projectile path, and logical sprite work buffers and images.
Hardware: Changes CPU-port $01 transiently by one decrement and a balancing increment to expose the required high-memory RAM; writes sprite work buffers, not VIC-II registers directly.

Finish the last slot of a composite sprite group, by marking its descriptor and restoring CPU-port banking: reached when the group's projectile slot is empty ($BCBF) and at the end of ConfigureCompositeSpriteSlot ($BD42) after a projectile has been drawn.
Inputs: X selects the logical sprite descriptor at $0218,X; the caller entered with $01 decremented to switch the I/O area out (RAM under $D000-$DFFF).
Outputs: Sets bit 6 in $0218,X, increments $01 to restore the caller's banking state, and returns.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, $0218,X, $01, and return-address stack bytes; X and Y are preserved.
Hardware: Restores CPU-port $01 banking by one increment; no VIC-II/CIA/SID register write.

Draw a projectile into one slot of a composite actor sprite. Inputs: X is the logical sprite slot (3 or 7) and Y the projectile slot (0 or 1); the projectile's kind $0280,Y and position $0284,Y/$0286,Y are valid and $01 has been lowered by the caller. Outputs: bit 3 of $0280,Y (the image phase) is toggled; $0220,X takes the attribute from $B90A; the image is the raw one that $B8EA/$B8FA point at or the packed sprite they name, unpacked into $02C0; $0295 or $0296 records the buffer in use; the sprite's X ($0200, with $0208 = 0) and Y ($0210) are the projectile's position plus the kind's offsets at $B919/$B920; $0238 and $F1 are cleared and $0271,Y takes $E2; the image is blitted into the slot's sprite, and FinishEmptyCompositeSpriteSlot sets bit 6 of $0218,X and puts $01 back. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite metadata and RAM, and increments the processor port $01 at the end.

Consume and prepare the next component of a composite sprite definition. Inputs: $02/$03 definition pointer, Y record cursor, and X slot. Outputs: the part is decoded or configured and X and Y advance. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and part scratch. Hardware: changes sprite RAM only.

Decode a compressed 63-byte sprite and place its part. Inputs: X slot, Y record cursor, and valid compressed-stream context. Outputs: decoded cache and configured part slot are produced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C5/$C6, and decoder and compositor scratch. Hardware: changes sprite RAM only.

Place one part of a frame and draw it into its sprite. Inputs: A chooses the source for the blitter (nonzero, the sprite just unpacked into $02C0; zero, the unpacked image at ($06)); $C5 the sprite slot; $C6 the part's offset in the frame record at ($02); $F1 the mirror flag and $97 the mirror width; the actor's position, $54/$55 for slots 0 to 3 and $56/$57 for slots 4 to 7. It selects the slot's sprite buffer ($BEC1), waits until bit 1 of the slot's flags at $0218 is clear, and sets the sprite's X ($0200/$0208: the actor's X plus the part's X offset less $30, or with $F1 set plus the mirror width less that offset), its Y ($0210, the actor's Y plus the part's Y offset) and its attributes ($0220, with bit 7, the multicolour flag, also in $0238). Then it falls into BlitSpritePartWithMask with A. Outputs: X = $C5, Y = $C6, left on the part's last byte (its attributes); A as BlitSpritePartWithMask leaves it. Clobbers: A, flags, $04/$05, $1F and $42-$44.

Draw a part into its slot's sprite at ($04), overwriting what is there: each of the 63 bytes is the source ANDed with a mask for its column ($42-$44), worked out from the sprite's X ($0200/$0208), which hides what lies past the right edge of the play window. With A nonzero the source is the sprite unpacked into $02C0 (BlitCachedSpriteMask, $BED7); with A zero, the image at ($06). When the mirror flag $F1 is set the bytes go through a reversal table with the outer columns swapped: for the image at ($06), the one at $1300 (hires) or $1200 (multicolour, when bit 7 of $0238 is set); for the unpacked sprite, always $1300. Then, when the sprite's Y ($0210) is below the line in $9E, it clears that many rows from the bottom, 21 at most. Outputs: X = $C5, Y = $C6, and A 0 or the difference $0210 less $9E. Clobbers: A, flags, $1F and $42-$44.

Select the backing buffer for a sprite slot. Inputs: X is sprite-slot index and slot flags are valid. Outputs: the destination pointer is installed in compositor zero page. Clobbers: A, flags, and destination pointer; X and Y are preserved.

Copy the sprite unpacked into $02C0 into the slot's sprite at ($04), each byte ANDed with the mask for its column ($42-$44): as it is, or, when the mirror flag $F1 is set, through the bit-reversal table at $1300 with the outer columns swapped. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.

Resolve and expand one tokenized sprite into the fixed 63-byte decode buffer, unless the alternate $C7 mode suppresses decoding
Inputs: A = sprite index; mode byte $C7; split source-pointer tables $CE54/$CF54 plus base $0E54; token stream at resolved $06/$07
Outputs: normal mode fills exactly $02C0-$02FE and returns A=$FF, X=$3F; tokens $69-$6F emit zero runs and $68 escapes a literal; alternate $C7 bit-6 mode adjusts pointer state and returns A=0 without filling the buffer
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, source pointer $06/$07, and decoder scratch

Expand a packed sprite into the 63-byte cache $02C0-$02FE from pointer $06/$07. Bytes $69-$6F emit 1-7 zeros; $68 escapes the following byte as one literal, including reserved values. Other bytes are literals. X counts output bytes; Y counts input bytes; return A=$FF. Every one of the 162 main-pool records expands to exactly 63 bytes and consumes precisely the distance to the next record.

Resolve the Central Park playable phase's alternate raw sprite pointer without decoding the 63-byte cache.
Inputs: A is the raw sprite's number; $C7 bit 6 selected raw-pointer mode before this entry.
Outputs: Stores in $06/$07 the address of that raw sprite, $F920 plus 64 times A, returns A=0, preserves X, and leaves $02C0-$02FE unchanged.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, V, Z, C, and $06/$07; X and the 63-byte cache are preserved.

Draw projectile slot 0 into the player's fourth sprite (slot 3), at most once per tick (update slot 9 of GateUpdateByTickInterval, which returns from the caller when no tick has passed). Inputs: slot-zero state at $0280, its position $0284/$0286, and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: when $0280 is nonzero its image (the phase flipped by bit 3 of $0280) is drawn at the projectile's position and masked behind the scenery; the projectile itself is not moved. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware: lowers the processor port $01 by one while it draws and puts it back; changes sprite RAM.

Draw projectile slot 1 into the enemy's fourth sprite (slot 7), at most once per tick (update slot 10 of GateUpdateByTickInterval, which returns from the caller when no tick has passed). Inputs: slot-one state at $0281, its position $0285/$0287, and shared object and sprite state. Outputs: when $0281 is nonzero its image (the phase flipped by bit 3 of $0281) is drawn at the projectile's position and masked behind the scenery; the projectile itself is not moved. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and sprite scratch. Hardware: lowers the processor port $01 by one while it draws and puts it back; changes sprite RAM.

Render the Central Park playable phase's projectile slot selected by Y into the last sprite of its group (slot 3 or 7), the common body of UpdateAuxSpriteSlot0 and UpdateAuxSpriteSlot1.
Inputs: Y is 0 for slot 0 or 1 for slot 1; $0280,Y and its position/type arrays are current; the caller's rate gate has passed.
Outputs: Returns if the slot is empty; otherwise lowers $01 to switch the I/O area out, draws the projectile into sprite slot Y*4+3 through ConfigureCompositeSpriteSlot (which puts $01 back), and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($9720) with the projectile's Y in A to hide it behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $01 transiently, $C5-$C7, sprite work buffers, and the masking routine's scratch.
Hardware: Decrements CPU-port $01 at $BF9D and restores it in the composition helper before the tail transfer; updates sprite work buffers but does not directly write VIC-II registers.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 0.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $C0D0-$C1A2, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=0 and tail-enters ObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 1.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $C0D0-$C1A2, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=1 and tail-enters ObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.

Invoke the spatial-object engine for object subtype/channel 2.
Inputs: Current area $A2, player position/heading, object records $C0D0-$C1A2, persistence $03D8+, and event-selected channel.
Outputs: Loads Y=2 and tail-enters ObjectEngine, which filters matching records and invokes callbacks/draw state.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6, $02/$03, object/animation/draw state, and callback-defined scratch.

Scan the current area's 14-byte object records for the requested mode, apply state/position/facing gates, and invoke eligible object callbacks
Inputs: Y = object mode/channel, stored to $C6; current area $A2; player position/facing; 14-byte records beginning at $C0D0; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y
Outputs: eligible callbacks at record bytes $C0D9/$C0DA are invoked through trampoline $C080; callback result controls continuation and object/presentation state may be updated
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $C6 and object-filter/callback/renderer scratch

Tail-dispatch to the handler selected from an object record. Inputs: $02/$03 is the handler address. Outputs: the handler returns directly to this routine's original caller. Clobbers: this dispatcher preserves registers and flags; the selected handler's contract applies. Hardware: handler-dependent.

Start the 100-tick timer of the found item shown in the panel: $A0 receives the tick $E2, or $FF when that is 0, and ExpireInactiveObjectAfterDelay ($C251) puts the selected item back 100 ticks later. When $A0 was 0 it first waits for raster line $FA and runs $C08E-$C0AD, which changes its own code: with $4E = $EE, $7A/$7B = $BFAD and $86/$87 = $BFB5, the two stores at $C092/$C094 write $DD into $C09B and $C0A3, the high bytes of SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4, so that pass reads CIA 2's timers through mirrors ($DD24, $DD86, $DDE4); the stores at $C0AB/$C0AD put $04 back, and the results of the reads are not kept. Inputs: $A0, tick $E2, pointers $7A/$7B and $86/$87, and $4E. Outputs: $A0. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and $A0. Hardware: reads VIC-II raster register $D012 and CIA 2's timer registers; writes no hardware register.

25-byte instruction continuation of $C083, including undocumented LAX absolute,Y at $C096. With Y = $4E = $EE, LAX loads both A and X from $DD24 (CIA 2's timer A low, through a mirror). The stores at $C092/$C094 have just changed the high bytes of the next two instructions ($C09B and $C0A3) from $04 to $DD, so SBC $0486 and CPX $04E4 run as SBC $DD86 and CPX $DDE4 (CIA 2's timer B low and timer A low); each selects whether an optional BIT $8A11 runs. Every path reaches LDA #4 and stores it through $7A/$86 at Y, which puts $04 back in $C09B and $C0A3. The comparisons change the path and its timing, not the stored value.

End of raster-synchronized object-state update: read the tick $E2, replace zero with $FF, save it as the active-object timestamp $A0, then return. The following $C0B8-$C0CF bytes are a pointer table; they are not instructions.

Six little-endian animation pointers through $C0C3. After object collection, $C062/$C069 compare the active player animation against these candidates using X=10,8,..0; a match replaces it with the parallel pointer at $C0C4/$C0C5 and doubles the player's animation delay countdown $58 (ASL $58).
High-byte indexed alias of the six animation words at $C0B8; paired comparisons use even X. This byte does not start a new array.

Six little-endian replacement animation words $C0C4-$C0CF, aligned with the match list at $C0B8. $C06E/$C073 install the matching replacement into $60/$61 and double the player's animation delay countdown $58; the table is followed by object records.
Odd-byte base of replacement animation pointers beginning $C0C4, selected with the matched even index X. The final word ends at $C0CF.

Negative $FF area sentinel ending the 15 fourteen-byte interaction records beginning at $C0D0; scanners stop before treating the following callback code as another record.

Accept the object callback only when the selected item $0279 is item 7, and then copy the first compiled collision record's start X ($FEF9) into its end X ($FEFB).
Inputs: Object-engine callback context and the selected item $0279.
Outputs: If $0279==7, copies $FEF9 to $FEFB and returns A=0 with Z set so object processing continues; otherwise returns with Z clear from the CMP (A holds $0279) so the engine skips the record's activation path.
Clobbers: A and flags; qualifying path writes $FEFB.

When object state $03DE is active, latch $03DB and set both paired state bytes $03DD/$03DE to $80.
Inputs: Object-engine callback context and state byte $03DE.
Outputs: If $03DE is nonzero, writes $03DB=$FF and $03DD=$03DE=$80; always returns A=0 so object processing continues.
Clobbers: A and flags; qualifying path writes $03DB/$03DD/$03DE.

Inputs: Object-engine callback context and state byte $03DD.
Outputs: If $03DD is nonzero, writes $03DB=$FF and $03DD=$03DE=$80; always returns A=0 so object processing continues.
Clobbers: A and flags; qualifying path writes $03DB/$03DD/$03DE.

When actor-state byte $70 equals 2, install enemy animation pointer $CE2A and set object/action flag $F8=2.
Inputs: Object-engine callback context and state byte $70.
Outputs: If $70==2, writes $62/$63=$CE2A through $AD3D, clears enemy animation delay/flags $5A/$5E, sets $F8=2, and returns A=0; otherwise returns the nonmatching state so object processing skips activation.
Clobbers: A, flags, $62/$63, $5A/$5E, and $F8.
