Draw the picture of the first object record of the current area ($A2) whose item is still in place. It scans the 14-byte records from $C0D0 to the $FF that ends them, passing over those of other areas, those whose item's flag ($03D8 plus the record's byte 11) is set, and those with no picture (bytes 5 and 6 of the record, a high byte of 0), and tail-enters the scene renderer ($8A86) with the first one left in $02/$03: at most one picture is drawn. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02/$03, and the renderer's scratch when it draws.

Expire a displayed inactive object after 100 engine ticks. Inputs: creation or display tick $A0 and current tick $E2. Outputs: the object remains or is cleared and its UI is refreshed. Clobbers: A, flags, and the clear helper's clobbers on expiry. Hardware: changes UI or display memory on expiry.

Remove the inactive-object display and redraw its status image. Inputs: current inactive-object and UI state. Outputs: $A0 is cleared and the corresponding UI image is rendered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible UI bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

The RTS that ends the Central Park playable phase's inactive-object expiry check. The branches at $C258 and $C25C come here when the delay has not elapsed or no inactive object is pending, and ClearInactiveObjectAndRefreshUi also ends here after redrawing the panel's image.
Inputs: A valid return address is on the stack.
Outputs: Returns; on the two branch paths nothing has been cleared or redrawn.
Clobbers: Registers, flags, object state, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.

Periodically render the alternating active-state image for the first eligible object in the current area
Inputs: timer slot 5; phase counter $A9; current area $A2; 14-byte records at $C0D0; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; two active scene pointers in record bytes 5-6 and 7-8
Outputs: on an admitted tick decrements $A9, selects one of the two active pointers by $A9 bit 0, loads it into $02/$03, and tail-enters the recursive renderer; clears $A9 and returns when no eligible object remains
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $A9, $02/$03, and scene-renderer scratch on a render path

Eight pointers, one for each kind of extra sprite the enemy can carry: none, $E979, $F1B2 and five times $F920. The extra sprite is not its weapon (the weapon is the frame's alternative slot, picked by the low two bits of $92, from the enemy's profile $72): for frames 0 to 48 the composer draws it in the enemy's first sprite, in place of the frame's first slot and at the position of its second, and sets the colours of the enemy's first three sprites from $E938. The high nibble of the area's entry in the enemy table at $B67F picks the pointer: it is twice the kind, a byte offset into this table. The composer ($BC2F-$BC5D) adds a word offset taken from the pose table at $E948 to the chosen pointer, reads the word there and unpacks the image it leads to, the same way for every kind. No area's enemy has a kind above 2, so the five pointers to $F920, the unpacked images, are never read.
The high bytes of the pointers at $E928: the composer reads the pair with the same Y, twice the kind.
Eight two-byte auxiliary attribute pairs, aligned with the group-base table at $E928. $BC82-$BC92 applies the selected pair to the companion logical sprite slots; the null group pair is zero.
Second byte indexed base of the eight paired auxiliary attribute records $E938-$E947. $BC82-$BC92 aligns each pair with its group pointer and applies attributes to companion sprite slots.

17 little-endian UI image pointers, read with twice image index at $B411-$B418. Entries share several images. Targets $3F40 and $FCC2-$FEA8 contain 4-by-2-cell image leaves. The final target, $FEF9, holds no image: it is where CompileCollision writes the walls of the area on screen, its first byte included. That byte is the first byte of the area's first compiled wall, $00 in this snapshot and for an area without walls but $78 in area 3, for one, so the size byte the renderer would read there changes from area to area.
